newsitem.title: ITALY: Credito Italiano sees 32 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Credito Italiano sees 32 pct profit growth.

text.p: Italian bank Credito Italiano SpA said on Thursday its parent net profit rose 32 percent in 1996 after it boosted income from services and made a sizeable reduction in personnel.
Credito said its net profit rose to 253.9 billion lire ($151 million) against 192 billion in 1995 while gross operating profit increased 20 percent to 1.08 trillion.
"Growth in services sales and a significant reduction of 802 employees confirm the value of our new strategy," the bank said, adding its staff now totalled 14,428.
Credito said it planned to pay an ordinary share dividend of 60 lire, up from 35 previously, and a savings share dividend of 75 lire against 50 in 1995.
Net commission from services rose 28.7 percent to 817 billion lire while financial operations swung into profit of 170 billion from a 28 billion loss in 1995.
The net profit came after several factors including write-downs of 203 billion and extraordinary income of 255 billion deriving mainly from share portfolio adjustment.

It said it would continue its programme of reorganising its holdings. In particular in the next few months a new consumer credit company, Credit Fiditalia, would become operative in partnership with French banking group Societe Generale.
